PJ-08
Deliver device identities, temporary-code enrollment, branch assignment, orientation/capabilities, revocation and safe reassignment.
in progress
Phase 2; PJ-03, reviewed D-03/D-07; FR-02/FR-03; PH-08/PH-09. 2026-10-19: the owner approved the server-side D-03 [device enrollment and lifecycle design](device-enrollment-design.md) and ADR-0027 under [PH-22](human-actions.md#ph-22) (PJ-33). Implemented per its [implementation status](device-enrollment-design.md#implementation-status): the `devices` API module, migration, contracts and SDK, `devices.view`/`devices.manage`, the branch-archive guard and the panel's Telas pages, with API integration and domain tests, browser component tests and an end-to-end journey with a simulated player. Remaining before completion: the Android player's enrollment, credential storage and erasure (PJ-12), hardware and orientation qualification (PH-08) and a device audit view.
PJ-09
Deliver tenant-safe validated private media, metadata, reusable asset references and deletion lifecycle.
in progress
Phase 2; PJ-03, reviewed D-05; FR-04; hardware profiles from PH-08. 2026-10-19: started on the owner's instruction to continue autonomously. The owner approved the D-05 [media library design](media-library-design.md) and ADR-0028 under [PH-23](human-actions.md#ph-23) (PJ-34) the same day. Implemented per its [implementation status](media-library-design.md#implementation-status), increments 1 and 2: the `media` API module with FFmpeg processing, migration, contracts and SDK, the four media capabilities, the trash and reference guards and the panel's Mídia pages, with API integration and domain tests against real FFmpeg, browser component tests and an end-to-end journey. Review fixes: profiles carry each view capability their media and screen actions need, released object files are unlinked only after the database change commits (also in the orphan sweep), stalled uploads end after 60 idle seconds, and video conversions start only with room for their rendition cap above the reserve. PJ-10, PJ-11, PJ-21 and PJ-20 register their reference guards (`playlist-draft`, `publication`, `catalog-record` and `layout-draft`). Remaining before completion: increment 3 (sharing with selected branches, storage accounting for PJ-27), playback qualification of the display profile on PH-08 hardware, and a provisioned media volume (PJ-13).
PJ-10
Deliver playlists, device/group assignments, regional schedules/defaults and preview with deterministic local-time rules.
in progress
Phase 2; PJ-08/PJ-09, D-06/D-10 contract/fixture review, FR-05/FR-06. PH-09 selected the [release policies](release-policies.md); implement their date/DST/coordination behavior and target-linked tests with PJ-20 rather than reopening unanswered owner choices. 2026-10-19: started on the owner's instruction to continue autonomously. The owner approved the D-06 [programming design](programming-design.md) and ADR-0029 under [PH-24](human-actions.md#ph-24) (PJ-35) the same day; implementation follows its delivery increments. Increment 1 is implemented per the design's [implementation status](programming-design.md#implementation-status): the `programming` API module with migration, contracts and SDK, the three programming capabilities, the explicit device time zone, the evaluator with canonical fixtures, timelines, guards and the move hook, with evaluator tests and a two-company integration suite. Increment 2 adds the panel's Programação pages (playlists, groups, schedules with API rule checks, seven-day previews, screen assignment with the unpublished confirmation) and the screen time zone setting, with browser component tests and an end-to-end journey. Review fixes: a per-company lock serializes the count limits; screen views hide a group or playlist the caller cannot fully see, while the timeline still shows what plays; the schedule editor offers every page of playlists. Full local gate (2026-10-19, continued in a later session on the review-fix head): `pnpm validate` passed with `CI=true` as in CI and a tmpfs `TMPDIR`, because the sandbox disk had less free space than the media volume reserve plus one conversion cap: frozen install, static, documentation and reference checks, 228 API tests including the Keycloak qualification and integration suites against real Keycloak and PostgreSQL and the media suites with real FFmpeg, 67 web unit tests, 68 browser component tests, build, bundle check, smoke and 27 E2E journeys. Table padding that an earlier commit had added to 17 unrelated documents was reverted. Increments 1 and 2 were merged to `main` through [pull request #11](https://github.com/GabriellMDias/teluni/pull/11) on 2026-10-20 after its CI passed. Remaining: increment 3 with PJ-11/PJ-20.
PJ-11
Deliver immutable publication, compatible device sync, version reconciliation and basic scoped monitoring/audit.
in progress
Phase 2; PJ-08/PJ-09/PJ-10, reviewed ADR-0019 and D-09/D-11; FR-07/FR-09; coordinate composition/catalog snapshots and price propagation with PJ-12/PJ-20/PJ-21. 2026-10-19: started on the owner's instruction to continue autonomously, stacked on the PJ-10 work of [pull request #11](https://github.com/GabriellMDias/teluni/pull/11). The owner approved the D-04 [publication and synchronization design](publication-sync-design.md) and ADR-0030 (PJ-36) under [PH-25](human-actions.md#ph-25) on 2026-10-20; implementation follows its recommended options per its delivery increments. Increment 1 is implemented per the design's [implementation status](publication-sync-design.md#implementation-status): the `publications` API module with migration, contracts, SDK and `TELUNI_SYNC_SIGNING_KEYS`, `publications.publish`, check/publish/history/restore with the reviewed content digest, exact protocol 1 manifests, the 30-second sync exchange with ES256 statements, delivery of the desired publication's manifest and renditions, screen states and transitions, the publication media guard, pruning after 90 days, and assignments that need confirmation only for unpublished destinations. Increment 2 adds the panel's Publicação section (review with counts, followers and blocking problems, publishing with the reviewed digest, history and restore, a step-up prompt), member screen states on group pages, the screen's synchronization section and list states in Telas, and assignments that confirm only unpublished destinations, with browser component tests and an end-to-end journey in which a simulated player verifies its statement, manifest and media. Full local `pnpm validate` passed on 2026-10-20 with `CI=true` and a tmpfs `TMPDIR` (the sandbox disk has less free space than the media reserve plus one conversion cap): 243 API tests, including 7 new domain and 7 new integration tests against real PostgreSQL, Keycloak and FFmpeg, 67 web unit tests, 74 browser component tests, build, bundle check, smoke and 28 E2E journeys. Review fixes: the `publication` media guard and the programming port's publication facts query through the caller's transaction, so they hold while the module is unmounted; screen synchronization reads answer `COMPANY_SUSPENDED` for suspended companies; statements stop listing reported publications once the desired one is active. Increments 1 and 2 were merged to `main` through [pull request #12](https://github.com/GabriellMDias/teluni/pull/12) on 2026-10-20 after its CI passed. Follow-up (2026-10-20): screen routes count their pre-authentication request limit per presented credential under a ceiling of 6,000 per address, because per address about 60 screens behind one router or proxy exhausted it; see the design's [implementation status](publication-sync-design.md#implementation-status). Increment 3 started the same day with the player: the sync response carries the screen zone's UTC offsets (three days back, 35 days ahead) and its rotation, and `apps/api/scripts/conformance.ts` writes the player [conformance fixtures](../../apps/api/test/publications/conformance.json), which a test keeps in step with the API's code. Remaining: player conformance on devices (PJ-12), layouts and catalogs (PJ-20/PJ-21) and commercial capping (PJ-27).
PJ-12
Deliver the Android TV player, durable staging/playback, offline scheduling, approved concurrent-content rendering, reboot/power-loss recovery and controlled packaging/updates.
in progress
Phase 2; reviewed ADR-0020 and D-03/D-04/D-07/D-11, PH-08 hardware and PJ-08/PJ-11/PJ-20 contracts; FR-08/FR-10 and playback acceptance. 2026-10-20: started under the owner's delegation after the D-07 [player design](player-design.md) and ADR-0031 (PJ-37). Increment 1 is implemented per the design's [implementation status](player-design.md#implementation-status): the sync response's zone offsets and rotation with the API's conformance fixtures (PJ-11 increment 3), and the Gradle build [`apps/player`](../../apps/player/README.md) with a JVM `core`. `core` holds the evaluator (every shared fixture, with the API's offsets), statement verification against the API's own statements, the strict manifest parser, trusted time, the atomic store, the device API checked against the OpenAPI document, the synchronization and staging engine and the playback planner, tested by 79 JVM tests. Review fixes: an unreadable credential erases local state; superseded and no-longer-desired staging attempts are collected; erasure stops staging and synchronization first; a schedule-only change activates below the reserve; media requests are paced and honor `RATE_LIMITED` under the per-credential limit of pull request #13; the trusted clock is synchronized. The Player CI job joins the required gate. Increment 1 was merged to `main` through [pull request #14](https://github.com/GabriellMDias/teluni/pull/14) on 2026-10-20 after its CI passed. Remaining: the Android `app` module (increment 2), which the cloud environment cannot build until [PH-26](human-actions.md#ph-26); qualification on [PH-08](human-actions.md#ph-08) hardware (increment 3); updates and credential rotation, with the signing key of [PH-27](human-actions.md#ph-27) (increment 4); and composition with PJ-20.
PJ-13
Prepare and verify pilot deployment, private ingress, off-host backups/restore, telemetry and host/endpoint migration procedures.
pending
Phase 1 planning already documented; Phase 2 delivery depends on PH-10, PH-13, reviewed ADR-0021 and working artifacts. No production changes authorized by this plan.
PJ-14
Run integrated release acceptance and the candidate customer pilot; record usability, offline/recovery, operating cost and support evidence.
pending
Phase 2 exit; PJ-03, PJ-08 through PJ-13 and PJ-20/PJ-21/PJ-24/PJ-27, applicable PJ-01/PH-06/PH-07/PH-08/PH-09/PH-11/PH-12/PH-13/PH-15–PH-19 prerequisites. PH-18 customer agreement precedes pilot entry; real costs are collected during the pilot and qualified before paid/public commitments, not fabricated as a pre-pilot result. No real-customer acceptance until the security/operations gates pass.
PJ-15
Evaluate further widgets, managed campaigns, analytics and presentation/catalog workflows beyond the approved initial release.
pending
Future Phase 3; PJ-14 evidence, separate scope/ADRs and implementation authorization. Freeform hybrid areas, regional schedules, multiple videos/audio and configurable typed catalogs are already FR-10/FR-11 and PJ-20/PJ-21.
PJ-16
Evaluate commercial expansion: integrations, fleet capabilities, other players, AI, automated subscriptions/payments, white-label and infrastructure scaling. Basic manual commercial access is PJ-27.

Future Phase 4; validated demand/costs and independent discovery

Local checks passed through `docs:references:check`, plus 67 web unit tests, 33 browser component tests, `build` and `smoke`; API reference generation, API tests and E2E journeys need a container runtime that was unavailable, so CI on the pull request is the remaining evidence. Organizations (PJ-03) now provides responsible administration with administrator approval and accepted responsibility transfer, explicitly expiring standard-role grants and company-customized profiles over the current organization capabilities; publication approvals and consent-based support remain. title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Status and scope
text:
Status and scope
**Approved detailed design for D-13, 2026-10-18.** The owner approved all ten [decisions for review](#decisions-for-review) as proposed, including ADR-0026, under [PH-21](human-actions.md#ph-21), and asked for implementation. Approval authorizes implementation in local and CI environments with synthetic addresses and Mailpit; [implementation status](#implementation-status) records what exists. It specifies company invitations (the selected invitation policy and IA-02) on top of the approved [tenant data design](tenant-data-design.md) and [identity and session design](identity-session-design.md), and the durable transactional-email mechanism they need, whose architectural direction [ADR-0026](../adr/0026-propose-a-postgresql-outbox-and-smtp-relay-for-transactional-email.md) proposes. The approved decisions are listed under [decisions for review](#decisions-for-review).
In scope: who may invite whom and with which access, the invitation lifecycle, the invitation credential and link, acceptance by a verified identity, revalidation, abuse limits, the outbound-mail outbox and dispatcher, SMTP delivery, failure handling, retention, observability and verification. Out of scope: account registration, email verification and password recovery, which Keycloak performs under D-02 and PJ-24; Keycloak's own mail delivery (see [Keycloak mail](#keycloak-mail)); choosing the real mail provider, sender domain and DNS authentication, which remain [PH-17](human-actions.md#ph-17); and legal retention periods, which remain [PH-13](human-actions.md#ph-13).

title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Policy inputs
text:
Policy inputs
The design applies these selected policies without changing them:
Company invitations are recipient-bound, single-use, revocable and valid for seven days; a resend invalidates the previous pending invitation; acceptance requires the matching authenticated identity and explicit membership confirmation; changing the recipient requires a new invitation ([identity and access](identity-and-access.md#enrollment-and-account-continuity)).
Email verification establishes mailbox control, not legal identity or company ownership, and accounts are never merged solely by equal email.
Company administrators invite with company scope; branch managers invite operators to their own branches without granting authority beyond their own ([permission matrix](identity-and-access.md#permission-model-and-default-matrix)). New administrators require the responsible administrator's approval (P10) with strong authentication no older than five minutes (P14). Temporary access expires explicitly and is never renewed automatically (P30).
Credentials in URLs are allowed only as short-lived, high-entropy, single-purpose values whose exposure is understood; reset and invitation links are `RESTRICTED` ([authentication policy](../security/authentication.md)). Retry, duplicate request, delivery failure and expiry must stay safe for email-based flows.
A durable required side effect records its intent in the same transaction as the change, and consumers tolerate duplicates ([delivery policy](../architecture/delivery-and-side-effects.md)).

title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Who may invite
text:
Who may invite
An invitation carries exactly one grant request with the same shape as a direct grant: a standard role, either the whole company or one to 100 explicit active branches of the company, and an optional grant expiry. The rules mirror direct grants:
Inviter
May invite
Conditions
Company administrator (strongly authenticated)
Operator or branch manager, company-wide or for any active branches
Company active
Responsible administrator
Additionally company administrator, always company-wide
Strong authentication no older than five minutes; the invitation is the P10 approval
Branch manager (strongly authenticated)
Operator only, for a subset of the branches the manager currently manages
Never company-wide, never another role
Operator
Nobody
—
A new capability, `invitations.manage`, is company-wide for administrators and branch-scoped for managers. Administrators see and manage every invitation of the company; a branch manager sees and manages only invitations whose whole branch scope lies inside the branches they currently manage. Invitation lists are paginated and cursor-bound like other company lists.
At invitation time the system never looks up principals by email: it neither reveals whether the address belongs to an account or a member nor links anything by address. The address binds only the later acceptance.

title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Invitation lifecycle
text:
Invitation lifecycle
PENDING ──accept──▶ ACCEPTED
   │ ├──revoke──▶ REVOKED
   │ ├──resend──▶ REPLACED   (a new PENDING invitation takes its place)
   │ └──7 days──▶ EXPIRED    (recorded lazily; an expired row is never accepted)

**Create.** Validates the recipient address (trimmed, at most 254 characters, one `@`, compared in lower case) and the grant request, then inserts the invitation, enqueues its email in the same transaction and writes one `invitation.created` audit event. A company has at most one pending invitation per normalized address (a partial unique index); creating another returns `INVITATION_PENDING`, and the panel offers resend instead.
**Resend.** Marks the pending invitation `REPLACED`, cancels its unsent email, and creates a new invitation with a new credential and a new seven-day validity, in one transaction. The old link stops working immediately.
**Revoke.** Marks the pending invitation `REVOKED` and cancels its unsent email. Revoking a final invitation is a no-op.
**Expire.** Validity ends seven days after creation. Reads treat an expired pending row as expired, and every invitation write in the company first records its expired pending rows as `EXPIRED`, so a new invitation to the same address is never blocked by an expired one and no scheduled job is needed for correctness.
**Accept.** See [acceptance](#acceptance). Acceptance is idempotent for the principal that accepted: repeating it returns the same result, so a lost response can be retried safely.
Every change writes its audit event in the same transaction. Audit details are allowlisted (invitation ID, role, scope, branch count, grant expiry, replaced invitation ID) and never contain the recipient address, so later erasure of the address does not require editing append-only audit rows.
Authority-changing writes follow tenant data design rule 5: the company row is locked first, then the invitation row, then the involved membership rows in ID order, and the actor's current access is rechecked inside the transaction.

title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Invitation credential and link
text:
Invitation credential and link
**Credential.** 32 bytes from the platform CSPRNG, encoded base64url. The invitation stores only its SHA-256 hash, under a unique index used for lookup. The credential is `RESTRICTED`: it never appears in logs, telemetry, errors, audit, analytics, query strings or the panel after acceptance.
**Delivery copy.** The email must contain the credential, so the outbox row keeps it encrypted with authenticated encryption under a dedicated outbound-mail key ring (key ID stored with the ciphertext, newest key first, older keys readable during rotation). The ciphertext is erased when the message reaches a final state (sent, failed or cancelled). After that, the credential is not recoverable from the database; a lost email is handled by resending, which issues a new credential.
**Link.** `{public origin}/invitations/accept#{credential}`. The fragment is never sent in HTTP requests or `Referer` headers. The panel reads it, keeps it in the tab's `sessionStorage`, removes it from the address bar with `history.replaceState`, and sends it only in the body of `POST` requests. Sign-in returns to `/invitations/accept` without the credential, and the panel resumes from `sessionStorage`; the stored value is cleared after acceptance, after a final error or when the tab closes.

title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Acceptance
text:
Acceptance
The invitee opens the link. Without a session, the page explains the invitation and offers sign-in through the existing login flow. Account registration, if the invitee has no account, is D-02's signup flow and is not designed here; until it exists, only people with an existing verified account can accept.
With a session, the panel calls a preview operation with the credential. It answers with the company display name, the role, the scope (branch names), any grant expiry, the invitation expiry and the inviter's display name, or with a failure. A preview has no effect.
The invitee explicitly confirms. The accept operation then, in one transaction:
finds the invitation by credential hash and locks its company row, the invitation row and the involved membership rows in that order; an unknown credential answers `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, and a final or expired one `INVITATION_NO_LONGER_VALID`;
requires that the session principal's verified email (identity's snapshot from the latest verified sign-in; sign-in already rejects unverified addresses) equals the recipient address case-insensitively, otherwise `INVITATION_RECIPIENT_MISMATCH`, which never reveals the invited address;
revalidates the invitation against current state: the company is active; the inviter is still an active member who could grant this role and scope now (for an administrator invitation, still the responsible administrator; for a manager's invitation, still managing every branch); every branch is still active. If anything fails, the invitation becomes invalid with `INVITATION_NO_LONGER_VALID` rather than being narrowed silently, and the inviter can issue a new one;
applies the membership rule below, inserts the grant with the inviter as grantor, marks the invitation `ACCEPTED`, and writes one `invitation.accepted` audit event.
Invitee's membership in the company
Result
None
A new active membership with the invited grant
Active
The invited grant is added to the existing membership (an identical effective grant is not duplicated)
Suspended
Refused with `MEMBERSHIP_SUSPENDED`; suspension is lifted only by an administrator, never by an invitation
Removed
A new active membership; the removed membership stays as history. The membership uniqueness rule becomes `UNIQUE (company_id, principal_id) WHERE status <> 'REMOVED'`
The invited role's assurance requirement still applies at use: an accepted administrator or branch-manager grant counts only in a strongly authenticated session, so the panel then offers step-up as it does today.

title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Durable email delivery
text:
Durable email delivery
[ADR-0026](../adr/0026-propose-a-postgresql-outbox-and-smtp-relay-for-transactional-email.md) sets the direction; this section specifies it.
**Ownership.** A new API module, `mail`, owns an `outbound_emails` table, the dispatcher and the SMTP adapter. It is platform-operational infrastructure without its own business meaning: producers own what a message means. Its public port lets a producer enqueue a message with a template key, locale, recipient, allowlisted parameters and an optional secret parameter inside the producer's own database transaction, and cancel a message it enqueued. Organizations is the first producer. The table has no tenant key because future producers (identity notices, platform messages) are not tenant-scoped; each row records its producer and producer reference, and invitation rows reference their message.
**Message states.** `PENDING` (waiting for a first or later attempt), `SENT`, `FAILED` (attempts exhausted or permanent rejection) and `CANCELLED` (cancelled by the producer before sending). A row records attempts, next attempt time, lease expiry, last failure class and the SMTP reply code, never the raw provider text or the message body.
**Dispatcher.** Runs inside the API process when the mail settings are configured, started after the server is ready and stopped during drain. Every few seconds, or when signalled after a commit in the same process, it claims a small batch with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`: due `PENDING` rows whose lease is absent or expired, setting a lease of two minutes and incrementing attempts. Several API instances can run it safely; the pilot runs one. For each message it decrypts the secret parameter, renders the templates and submits through SMTP with connection and total timeouts of 30 seconds. Shutdown stops claiming, lets in-flight sends finish within the drain deadline, and leaves the rest to lease expiry.
**Outcomes and retries.**
SMTP outcome
Result
Accepted (2xx after `DATA`)
`SENT`, secret erased
Permanent rejection (5xx)
`FAILED` immediately, secret erased
Transient failure (4xx, connection, TLS or timeout)
Retry after about 1, 5, 15 and 60 minutes, then 3, 6 and 12 hours, with jitter; `FAILED` after the 8th attempt (about 22 hours, well inside the seven-day invitation)
Retries use the same `Message-ID`, derived from the message ID, so mail clients can recognize repeats. Delivery is at least once: a crash after the relay accepted a message but before `SENT` was recorded sends it again when the lease expires. A duplicate invitation email carries the same still-valid link, so the duplicate is harmless. Bounces after acceptance by the relay and provider webhooks are not handled in this version; the panel shows "sent" as "handed to the mail service", not as delivered.
**Panel feedback.** The invitation list shows each pending invitation's delivery state (waiting, sent, or failed) and offers resend and revoke. A failed delivery never silently disappears.
**Failure windows.** Committing the invitation and its message together closes the commit/publication gap. The relay-accepted/not-recorded gap is the accepted duplicate above. A revoke racing an in-flight send can deliver a link that no longer works, which acceptance rejects. Losing the database after `SENT` loses nothing a resend cannot recreate.
**Transport.** SMTP submission with authentication through the established `nodemailer` library, pinned like other dependencies. Production requires implicit TLS or mandatory STARTTLS with certificate verification; plaintext SMTP is accepted only for loopback or test sinks outside production. The relay is provider-neutral, so PH-17 can choose any service that offers authenticated SMTP submission, and changing provider is a configuration change.
**Configuration concepts.** Relay host and port, TLS mode, username, password (`RESTRICTED`), sender address and display name, and the outbound-mail key ring (`RESTRICTED`). Names are added to the canonical configuration schema when implemented. Like other module requirements, mail stays unmounted outside production until configured, and production refuses to start when a module that requires mail is composed without it. Invitations require mail.
**Observability.** Metrics: messages by state, age of the oldest due `PENDING` message, attempts, send latency, and failures by class. Logs and traces carry message, producer and invitation IDs, never recipient addresses, credentials or bodies. Alert thresholds and channels remain D-09; until then, the oldest pending age and failure counts are visible through metrics.

title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Keycloak mail
text:
Keycloak mail
Keycloak sends its own verification and recovery email synchronously, through the SMTP settings the realm provisioning script writes, and the person can request it again. Teluni configures Keycloak with the same relay and sender. Those messages do not pass through the outbox, and their durability remains Keycloak's behavior, qualified under PJ-24.

Data and retention
Data
Classification

title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Verification
text:
Verification
Integration tests against migrated PostgreSQL, the synthetic two-company fixture and a disposable Mailpit:
IA-02: the verified recipient accepts once within seven days; a wrong recipient, replay by another principal, and revoked, replaced or expired invitations fail; a repeated acceptance by the same principal returns the same result; no account is linked by email.
Inviter scope: managers cannot invite beyond operators or outside their branches; non-responsible administrators cannot invite administrators; stale assurance is rejected; cross-company identifiers answer not found.
Revalidation: acceptance fails after the inviter loses authority or responsibility, after a branch is archived and after company suspension; nothing is narrowed silently.
Membership cases: none, active, suspended and removed, with the partial uniqueness rule.
Atomicity: a failed invitation insert enqueues no message; revoke and resend cancel unsent messages; audit events commit exactly once.
Delivery: Mailpit receives the rendered `pt-BR` and `en-US` messages with a working link; injected 4xx, 5xx, timeout and crash-after-accept cases follow the retry table; competing dispatchers never send one claim twice; secrets are erased at final states; no address or credential appears in captured logs.
Limits and retention: the per-company, pending and per-address limits; cleanup removes rows on schedule.
A browser journey sends an invitation, reads the message from Mailpit, signs in as the recipient, accepts and sees the company; a second identity with a different address is refused.

Decisions for review
The owner approved each item as proposed on 2026-10-18 under [PH-21](human-actions.md#ph-21):
**Delivery architecture (ADR-0026).** Application-owned transactional email through a PostgreSQL outbox written in the producer's transaction, an in-process dispatcher in the API, and a provider-neutral authenticated SMTP relay through `nodemailer`; no message broker, separate worker service, provider HTTP API or webhook in this version.
**Delivery guarantees.** At least once, with possible duplicates after a crash; up to eight attempts over about 22 hours, immediate failure on permanent rejection, and failures shown to the inviter, who can resend.
**Invitation credential.** 256-bit random credential, stored only as a hash; an encrypted copy for delivery under a dedicated key ring, erased at the message's final state; link credential in the URL fragment, removed from the address bar and kept in the tab's session storage during sign-in.
**Acceptance identity.** The session principal's verified email must equal the recipient address case-insensitively, with explicit confirmation; principals are never looked up by email at invitation time; until D-02 signup exists, only people with an existing verified account can accept.
**Membership cases.** An active member gains the invited grant; a suspended member is refused; a removed person returns as a new membership, which changes membership uniqueness to exclude removed memberships.
**Revalidation at acceptance.** The inviter must still be able to grant the invited role and scope, the company and every branch must be active; otherwise the invitation becomes invalid rather than narrowed. A responsibility transfer therefore invalidates the former responsible administrator's pending administrator invitations.
**Who invites.** Administrators invite operators and branch managers; only the responsible administrator, with five-minute strong authentication, invites administrators; branch managers invite operators within their own branches; invitations can carry a grant expiry; one pending invitation per company and address, and resend replaces it.
**Abuse limits and content.** 50 invitations per company per 24 hours, 100 pending per company, 3 invitation emails per address per 24 hours across Teluni; no free-text message; fixed `pt-BR`/`en-US` templates in the company's default locale.
**Retention (provisional until PH-13).** Encrypted credential erased at final state; outbound message rows deleted 30 days after their final state; invitation recipient addresses replaced by a tombstone 90 days after the invitation becomes final; audit events never store the address.
**Keycloak mail.** Keycloak keeps sending its own verification and recovery mail synchronously through the same relay, outside the outbox.
Approving these items authorizes implementation in local and CI environments with synthetic addresses and Mailpit. It does not choose the real mail provider or sender domain (PH-17), set legal retention (PH-13) or authorize sending to real people.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Status and scope
text:
Status and scope
**Approved detailed design for D-05, 2026-10-19.** The owner approved all nine [decisions for review](#decisions-for-review) as proposed under [PH-23](human-actions.md#ph-23), including ADR-0028, after asking for development to continue autonomously. Approval authorizes implementation of PJ-09 in local and CI environments with generated fixtures.
In scope: tenant-owned media assets and their branch scope, upload, trustworthy inspection and validation against AT-02/AT-03, the playback rendition profile and conversion (FR-04), processing isolation, private storage and delivery to the panel, archive, trash and reference-safe purge (AT-17), permissions, abuse limits, audit, data, contracts, panel workflow and verification.
Out of scope, with their owners: delivery of renditions to devices inside publications (D-04, PJ-11); playlists and other references to media (PJ-10, PJ-20, PJ-21), which register through the reference port defined here; commercial original-media quotas and the 80%/100% warnings (PJ-27); qualifying any device decoder, memory or storage profile (PH-08, PJ-12); malware scanning and content moderation (pending risk decision, PH-13); the production container image that ships FFmpeg (PJ-13).

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Policy inputs
text:
Policy inputs
The design applies these selected policies without changing them:
Validate declared and inspected type, size, decoded dimensions, duration, compatibility and scoped references; enforce all bounds, not only compressed size: images at most 20 MiB, each decoded axis at most 8,192 px and at most 32,000,000 pixels (AT-02); videos at most 1 GiB and 60 minutes (AT-03). Ingestion bounds are configurable engineering defaults, not plan quotas.
Preserve originals and create compatible renditions when validated processing is supported; show preparation, progress and preview; reject with an actionable reason when safe conversion is unavailable; never silently distort content ([media lifecycle](release-policies.md#media-and-deletion-lifecycle)).
Archiving removes media from new selections without breaking references. Physical deletion is blocked while drafts, active, staged or recovery generations or protected publications reference the media, disclosing only references the caller may see; a recoverable archive or trash lasts at least 30 days before purge (AT-17).
Uploading media is allowed to administrators company-wide and to branch managers and operators in their branches; archive and restore to administrators and branch managers; permanent deletion only to administrators ([permission matrix](identity-and-access.md#permission-model-and-default-matrix)). Share media explicitly with branches or the whole company and enforce scope on lists, previews and downloads, not only on buttons.
Customer media is `CONFIDENTIAL`, private, never public because it appears on a screen, and never addressed by a public filesystem path or a permanent bearer URL ([operations](operations.md#persistent-state-and-storage-portability)). Uploads are not executable content; parsers run isolated ([security requirements](security-and-i18n.md#media-and-audit-protections)).
Media storage is a media-owned capability with replaceable filesystem I/O so that an S3-compatible store can be added later (ADR-0021).

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Assets, scope and visibility
text:
Assets, scope and visibility
An **asset** is one uploaded file and what Teluni derived from it. It belongs to one company and has an owning scope:
**Company** (`branch_id` empty): created by people with company-wide upload authority. Every member with `media.view` anywhere in the company can see and use it; this is the "shared with the whole company" case.
**Branch**: created for one branch. Members with `media.view` on that branch see and use it; others do not learn it exists (`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`).
Explicit sharing of a branch asset with further selected branches is a later increment of this design (a `media_asset_shares` table with read/use authority only); until then a company-scoped asset is the way to share. Editing authority always follows the owning scope.
Each asset has a name (1 to 120 characters, the uploaded file name by default, never used as a path), a kind (`IMAGE` or `VIDEO`), an optional set of up to 10 tags (each 1 to 40 characters) for organization and search, and the inspected facts: content type, size, width, height, duration and whether it has audio.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Upload
text:
Upload
Upload is two requests, so the server can admit the file before receiving any bytes and the bytes stream to disk without buffering:
`POST /companies/{companyId}/media` with the name, scope, declared content type and declared size creates the asset in `UPLOADING`. The server requires `media.upload` on the scope, an active company and branch, a declared type from the allowlist below and a declared size within the kind's limit, and checks the abuse limits and the storage reserve.
`PUT /companies/{companyId}/media/{assetId}/content` with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` and a `Content-Length` equal to the declared size streams the bytes to a temporary file on the media volume while computing their SHA-256. More bytes than declared, fewer bytes, a closed connection or a size mismatch delete the temporary file and leave the asset in `UPLOADING`, so the person can retry the same `PUT`. A complete upload moves the asset to `PROCESSING` and wakes the processor.
An asset still in `UPLOADING` one hour after creation is discarded by maintenance. Resumable chunked upload (for example the tus protocol) is not part of this design; it is the preferred extension if pilot measurements show that whole-file retries of large videos are a problem.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Inspection and validation
text:
Inspection and validation
Every check runs on the server; the declared values only admit the upload.
**Signature.** The first bytes must carry the signature of an allowed format, and that format must match the declared type: JPEG (`FF D8 FF`), PNG (the 8-byte PNG signature), WebP (`RIFF....WEBP`), the ISO base media family (`ftyp` box: MP4, MOV, M4V) or Matroska/WebM (EBML header). Anything else, including a mismatch with the declared type, is rejected as `MEDIA_TYPE_MISMATCH` or `MEDIA_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED`.
**Probe.** `ffprobe` reads the file with its demuxer forced to the format the signature identified, input limited to the local file protocol, and JSON output bounded to 1 MiB. A probe that fails, times out or reports no usable stream rejects the asset as `MEDIA_UNREADABLE`.
**Images.** Exactly one still picture coded as JPEG, PNG or WebP; animated PNG or WebP is rejected. Each axis at most 8,192 px and at most 32,000,000 pixels, after applying the EXIF orientation.
**Videos.** At least one video stream whose codec is H.264, HEVC, VP8, VP9, AV1 or MPEG-4 Part 2; audio, when present, AAC, MP3, Opus, Vorbis, FLAC or AC-3. Each axis at most 8,192 px, frame rate at most 120 fps, duration more than 0 and at most 3,600 seconds (AT-03). Further streams (subtitles, data, attachments) are ignored and never copied.
**Decode.** Producing the renditions decodes the whole file. A decoding error rejects the asset as `MEDIA_UNREADABLE`; the original is never offered for use in that case.
A rejection is final for that asset: it moves to `REJECTED` with the reason code, its temporary and derived files are deleted, and the panel explains the reason in the person's language. The person may discard it.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Renditions and the playback profile
text:
Renditions and the playback profile
The original is kept unchanged and is never sent to a screen. Each asset gets a **display** rendition, which is what playlists and publications use, and a **thumbnail** for the panel:
Kind
Display rendition
Thumbnail
Image
JPEG (or PNG when the image has transparency), EXIF orientation applied, all metadata removed (including location), scaled down without enlargement to fit 3840×2160 for landscape or 2160×3840 for portrait
JPEG fitting 320×320
Video
MP4 with the index at the start, H.264 High profile level 4.1, 8-bit 4:2:0, at most 1920×1080 for landscape or 1080×1920 for portrait, at most 30 fps, rotation applied, metadata removed; audio AAC-LC stereo 48 kHz at 128 kbit/s when the original has audio
JPEG fitting 320×320 from the frame at one second (or the middle of shorter videos)
A video that already matches the profile (H.264 High, Main or Baseline at or below level 4.1, 8-bit 4:2:0, within the size and frame-rate bounds, AAC or no audio, no rotation) is remuxed without re-encoding, so it keeps its quality. Everything else is transcoded with `libx264` (preset `veryfast`, constant quality 21). The result is probed again and must match the profile before the asset becomes `READY`.
This profile is the conservative reference that Android TV hardware decoders commonly support and matches the AT-04 reference qualification (1080p output, two simultaneous 1080p/30 fps videos). It is not a support claim: PH-08 and PJ-12 qualify real devices, and a later profile (for example 4K HEVC) is an additional rendition with its own evidence, never a silent replacement. Output larger than 2 GiB, a transcode slower than the processing timeout or a profile violation after conversion rejects the asset as `MEDIA_CONVERSION_FAILED` with the advice to export a smaller or shorter file.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Processing and isolation
text:
Processing and isolation
**Processor.** An in-process processor, like the mail dispatcher, claims assets in `PROCESSING` from PostgreSQL with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and a lease, and runs one job at a time by default (`TELUNI_MEDIA_PROCESSING_CONCURRENCY`, 1 to 4). Several API processes can share one database. Interrupted work (crash, restart, lease expiry) is picked up again; an internal failure retries up to three times with backoff and then moves the asset to `FAILED`, which the panel shows as "could not be prepared, try again or contact support".
**Isolation.** Untrusted bytes are parsed only by `ffprobe` and `ffmpeg`, never inside the API process. Each runs as a separate child process with an empty environment except `PATH`, a fixed argument list (no shell), inputs and outputs only inside the job's temporary directory, the file protocol only (no network or other protocols), stdin closed, bounded stderr capture, and a wall-clock timeout: 30 seconds for a probe, 120 seconds for an image, and 120 seconds plus four times the video duration for a video (at most four hours), after which the process group is killed. Where the host provides `prlimit`, each child also gets address-space and CPU-time limits. Container-level confinement (non-root user, read-only root filesystem, no network for a separate processing container) belongs to the deployment work in PJ-13.
**Tools.** FFmpeg is an external executable found at `TELUNI_MEDIA_FFMPEG_PATH` and `TELUNI_MEDIA_FFPROBE_PATH` (default `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` on `PATH`), version 6.1 or later. At startup the module checks both; in production a missing or older tool stops the start, elsewhere processing stays queued and an error is logged.
**Progress.** The asset stores the processing stage (`probing`, `converting`, `verifying`) and, while converting a video, the percentage reported by FFmpeg's progress output, at most once per two seconds. The panel polls the asset while it is processing.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Storage
text:
Storage
**Volume.** Media lives under the directory in `TELUNI_MEDIA_STORAGE_PATH`, which must be an absolute path on a durable mount outside disposable containers (ADR-0021). Setting it activates the media module. The directory holds `objects/` and `work/`; both must be on the same filesystem so a finished file is published with an atomic rename.
**Objects.** Every stored file is an immutable object named by the SHA-256 of its bytes inside its company: `objects/{companyId}/{first two hex digits}/{sha256}`. The same bytes uploaded twice by one company are stored once; companies never share objects, so storage never reveals whether another company holds a file. A `media_objects` row per company and hash records size and type and is the lock that keeps publication and purge consistent.
**Writes.** A finished file is written to `work/`, flushed to disk, and then, inside a transaction that holds the object row's lock, renamed into place before the referencing asset row commits. Releasing an object deletes its row under the same lock and unlinks the file only after that transaction commits, again under the lock and only while no row exists. A crash or rollback can therefore leave an unreferenced file, never a reference without a file. Maintenance deletes `work/` entries older than one day and object files without a row.
**Reads.** The database is the authority: a read resolves the asset, checks authorization and only then opens the object by hash. File paths, hashes and the storage directory never appear in responses, errors, logs or audit.
**Reserve.** Uploads are refused with `MEDIA_STORAGE_FULL` when the free space of the media volume would fall below the larger of 2 GiB and 10% of the volume, so a full disk never corrupts published media or stops the database. A video conversion starts only while the reserve still holds with room for the rendition cap of every running conversion; otherwise it fails and retries with backoff. This protects the host; it is not the commercial quota.
**Portability.** A later S3-compatible store implements the same small object interface (`put` from a finished temporary file, `open` with an optional byte range, `delete`, `list` for reconciliation), keeping object identity and domain rules unchanged.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Delivery to the panel
text:
Delivery to the panel
`GET /companies/{companyId}/media/{assetId}/content?variant=thumbnail|display|original` streams the variant to an authenticated session with `media.view` on the asset (`original` needs `media.upload` on the asset's scope, since it may carry metadata the renditions removed). Responses are `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` with the object hash as a strong `ETag` (so revalidation is cheap and revocation applies on the next request), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox; default-src 'none'`, the server-determined content type, `Content-Disposition` (`inline` for renditions, `attachment` with a sanitized name for the original), and single-range `Range` support for video seeking. Delivery to screens is defined with publications (PJ-11) and uses the device credential, never the panel route.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Lifecycle
text:
Lifecycle
 create      upload complete       processing ok
───────▶ UPLOADING ───────▶ PROCESSING ───────▶ READY ◀──────▶ ARCHIVED ───────▶ DELETED ───────▶ PURGED
            │                  │   │              archive / restore   delete        (30 days, no
            │ 1 h idle         │   └─▶ FAILED                         ▲  restore     protected
            ▼                  ▼                                      │  ◀────────   references)
        discarded           REJECTED ── discard ──▶ discarded

**Rename and tags.** `media.upload` on the asset's scope and the expected version, in any state but `DELETED` and `PURGED`.
**Archive and restore.** `media.archive` on the scope. An archived asset disappears from selection lists and keeps working wherever it is already used.
**Delete.** Only from `ARCHIVED`, with `media.delete` (administrators) and a confirmation naming the asset. The server asks every registered reference guard whether a protected reference exists (drafts, active, staged or recovery generations, protected publications); if one does, it answers `MEDIA_IN_USE` and nothing changes. Listing the references the caller may see arrives with the first referencing module (PJ-10), which owns their names. Otherwise the asset becomes `DELETED` with `purge_after` 30 days later (AT-17), hidden from everyone but administrators' trash view.
**Restore from trash.** `media.delete` before `purge_after`; the asset returns to `ARCHIVED`.
**Purge.** Maintenance takes `DELETED` assets past `purge_after`, asks the reference guards again, and only when nothing protects the asset marks it `PURGED`, clears its object references and deletes each object no other asset of the company references. A protected asset stays `DELETED` and is retried; retention expiry alone never deletes media, as the release policies require. The `PURGED` row keeps the ID, name and dates for audit; its bytes are gone.
**Discard.** An asset in `UPLOADING`, `REJECTED` or `FAILED` was never usable, so a person with `media.upload` on its scope can discard it immediately; it becomes `PURGED` and its files are deleted.
**Reference port.** The media module exposes `registerReferenceGuard(kind, guard)` on its public port. A guard runs in the deleting or purging transaction after the asset row is locked and returns the references it knows, each with the branch it belongs to, so the media module can disclose only what the caller may see. Programming (PJ-10), publications (PJ-11), compositions (PJ-20) and catalogs (PJ-21) register their guards when they exist. Selecting media for a new reference goes through the port's `requireSelectable`, which accepts only `READY` assets the caller may use.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Permissions
text:
Permissions
Four capabilities are added to the organizations domain, which owns role presets and delegable profile capabilities:
Capability

`media.view`: list, search, preview and use assets
Company
Granted branches and company assets

`media.upload`: upload, rename, tag, discard unusable uploads, download originals

`media.view`, `media.upload` and `media.archive` are delegable in company-customized profiles; `media.delete` is not, because the matrix gives permanent deletion only to administrators. Company-scoped assets are viewable through any `media.view` grant in the company, but uploading, editing or archiving them needs the capability company-wide. Hidden assets answer `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Abuse limits
text:
Abuse limits
Proposed initial values, each answering `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`:
At most 5 assets in `UPLOADING` per person and 20 per company.
At most 200 asset creations per company per day.
At most 20 assets in `PROCESSING` per company, so one company cannot monopolize the processor.
The upload `PUT` has no request-size limit beyond the declared size, a 2-hour request timeout and an idle timeout of 60 seconds without bytes.
Commercial original-media quotas (2 GiB trial, 10 GiB paid) and their warnings arrive with PJ-27, which will count each original object once per company as the commercial policies require; the creation request is where admission will be checked.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Data
text:
Data
All tables belong to the media module, with Prisma models in `prisma/schema/media.prisma`, semantic metadata, runtime grants and one reviewed migration.
Table
Contents
Notes
`media_objects`
`(company_id, sha256)` key, byte size, content type, created time
One row per stored file per company; publication and purge serialize on a transaction-scoped advisory lock per object
`media_assets`
`(company_id, id)`, optional composite `(company_id, branch_id)` reference, name, tags, kind, status, rejection reason, declared type and size, original/display/thumbnail object hashes (composite references to `media_objects`), inspected facts, processing stage/progress/attempts/lease, created-by membership, created/ready/archived/deleted/purge-after/purged times, version
Composite tenant references; runtime role never updates `company_id` or `branch_id`
`media_audit_events`
Company, actor, action, target asset, allowlisted details
Append-only; `media.created`, `media.uploaded`, `media.ready`, `media.failed`, `media.rejected`, `media.renamed`, `media.tagged`, `media.archived`, `media.restored`, `media.deleted`, `media.trash_restored`, `media.purged`, `media.discarded`. Details hold IDs, kinds, sizes and reason codes, never file names of other assets, hashes or paths
Names, tags, inspected facts and the stored bytes are `CONFIDENTIAL`. The original file name is used as the default name only; it is not stored separately.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Contracts
text:
Contracts
Human operations (session access, CSRF as elsewhere): `GET /companies/{companyId}/media` (paginated, cursor-bound; filters by kind, status, scope, tag and name text), `POST .../media` (create), `GET .../media/{assetId}`, `PUT .../media/{assetId}/content` (upload bytes), `GET .../media/{assetId}/content` (download a variant), `PATCH .../media/{assetId}` (name, tags, expected version), `POST .../media/{assetId}/archive`, `.../restore`, `.../delete`, `.../restore-deleted` and `DELETE .../media/{assetId}` (discard). All are TypeBox contracts in the OpenAPI document; the shared module contract gains the `application/octet-stream` request body and a binary response so the document describes them. The web uses the generated SDK except for the upload body, which it sends with `XMLHttpRequest` to report progress. New expected errors: `MEDIA_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED`, `MEDIA_TOO_LARGE`, `MEDIA_UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE`, `MEDIA_NOT_UPLOADING`, `MEDIA_NOT_READY`, `MEDIA_IN_USE`, `MEDIA_STORAGE_FULL`, `MEDIA_INVALID_STATE`, plus the existing `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, `RESOURCE_VERSION_CONFLICT`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `VALIDATION_FAILED` and access errors. Rejection reasons (`MEDIA_TYPE_MISMATCH`, `MEDIA_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED`, `MEDIA_TOO_LARGE`, `MEDIA_DIMENSIONS_EXCEEDED`, `MEDIA_DURATION_EXCEEDED`, `MEDIA_UNREADABLE`, `MEDIA_CONVERSION_FAILED`) are a closed enumeration on the asset, not HTTP errors.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Panel
text:
Panel
A **Media** view per company (pt-BR "Mídia") shows a grid of thumbnails with name, kind, duration or dimensions, scope and state, with filters by kind, scope, tag and state and a name search, limited to what the person may view. **Upload** accepts several files (button or drag and drop), asks for the scope when the person may upload to more than one, shows per-file progress and then the preparation state, and explains rejections. The asset page shows the preview (image, or video with controls), facts, scope, tags and history of state, and offers rename, tags, archive and restore, delete with a confirmation naming the asset, and download of the original where allowed. Administrators see a **Trash** filter with restore. Copy is in `pt-BR` and `en-US`.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Verification
text:
Verification
Domain unit tests: signature detection, declared-type matching, probe interpretation for every bound (axis, pixels, duration, frame rate, codecs, animation), the remux-or-transcode decision, lifecycle transitions and permission decisions.
Processing tests with real FFmpeg against generated fixtures: JPEG with EXIF orientation and location metadata (rotated and stripped), PNG with transparency, oversized and over-pixel images, animated WebP, a spoofed extension, truncated and corrupted files, a polyglot file, compliant H.264 (remuxed), HEVC and VP9 (transcoded), portrait video with rotation metadata, a video over 60 minutes declared as short (rejected from the probe), and a timeout.
Integration tests against PostgreSQL with two companies and differently scoped members: creation and upload allowed and denied by scope, company assets visible to branch members but not editable, ID substitution across companies, cursors, versions, size mismatch and interrupted uploads, abuse limits, concurrent processing claims, reference guards blocking delete and purge, purge after 30 days keeping objects still used by another asset, and audit rows.
Delivery tests: authorization on every variant, range requests, headers, and no route answering for another company's asset.
Browser component tests for the library, upload progress and the delete confirmation, and one end-to-end journey: upload an image and a video, wait until ready, preview, archive, delete and restore from trash.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Delivery increments
text:
Delivery increments
Module, schema, migration, configuration, object store, upload, inspection, processor, renditions, list, detail, delivery, rename, tags, archive and restore, audit and the panel library with upload and preview.
Delete to trash, restore from trash, purge, reference port and guards, discard, maintenance (expired uploads, work files, orphan objects) and the trash view.
Explicit sharing with selected branches, storage accounting per company for PJ-27 and the end-to-end journey hardening.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Implementation status
text:
Implementation status

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Decisions for review
text:
Decisions for review
The owner approved each item as proposed on 2026-10-19 under [PH-23](human-actions.md#ph-23):
**Storage (ADR-0028).** Media on a configured local directory behind a media-owned object interface; immutable objects named by SHA-256 per company, deduplicated only within a company; atomic publish by rename under a database lock; the database is the authority; a free-space reserve of max(2 GiB, 10%).
**Processing tool and isolation (ADR-0028).** FFmpeg 6.1 or later as an external executable for probing, image and video renditions, run as child processes with no shell, a scrubbed environment, file-only protocol, forced demuxers, timeouts and optional `prlimit`; no image library inside the API process; an in-process PostgreSQL-leased processor with concurrency 1 by default.
**Accepted inputs.** Images JPEG, PNG and static WebP; videos in MP4/MOV or Matroska/WebM with H.264, HEVC, VP8, VP9, AV1 or MPEG-4 Part 2 video and AAC, MP3, Opus, Vorbis, FLAC or AC-3 audio; AT-02/AT-03 bounds plus at most 8,192 px per axis and 120 fps for video.
**Playback profile.** One display rendition per asset: H.264 High 4.1, at most 1080p30, AAC-LC stereo, MP4 faststart, remuxed when already compliant; images as JPEG or PNG within 3840×2160 with orientation applied and all metadata removed; originals kept but never sent to screens. Higher profiles only with device evidence.
**Upload transport.** A create request that admits the upload, then one streamed `PUT` of the whole file with an exact declared size; no resumable protocol now.
**Scope and permissions.** Company or single-branch ownership; `media.view`, `media.upload`, `media.archive` and `media.delete` as in the table, with `media.delete` administrators only and not delegable; explicit multi-branch sharing in a later increment.
**Lifecycle and purge.** Archive and restore; delete only from archive, blocked by protected references through registered guards; 30-day trash with restore; purge rechecks references and deletes objects no other asset uses; unusable uploads discarded immediately.
**Abuse limits.** 5 open uploads per person and 20 per company, 200 creations per company per day, 20 processing per company.
**Retention (provisional until PH-13).** Unfinished uploads discarded after one hour; rejected and failed assets kept until discarded; deleted assets purged no earlier than 30 days after deletion; purged rows and audit kept with the company.
Approval authorizes implementation of PJ-09 in local and CI environments with generated fixtures. It does not qualify any device profile (PH-08), select malware scanning or moderation (PH-13), or build the production image (PJ-13).

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Alternatives considered
text:
Alternatives considered
**`sharp` (libvips) for images.** Fast and well maintained, but it parses untrusted images inside the API process and adds a native dependency next to FFmpeg, which the videos need anyway. FFmpeg 6.1 applies EXIF orientation and strips metadata, so one isolated tool covers both kinds.
**Object storage (S3-compatible, for example MinIO) now.** It would separate storage from the host, but adds a service to operate on a single-host pilot with no budget. ADR-0021 already keeps the interface replaceable.
**Storing media in PostgreSQL large objects.** Transactional, but it inflates backups and database I/O with gigabytes of video and makes range reads and streaming harder.
**Global deduplication across companies.** Saves space but lets one company infer that another holds a given file and couples tenant deletion; per-company deduplication keeps tenants independent.
**Resumable uploads (tus) now.** Better for unstable connections, but adds a protocol and its state; deferred until measurements show the need.
**Sending originals to screens and relying on device decoders.** Avoids conversion, but makes playback depend on every device's codec support, which FR-04 and the release policies rule out.
**A separate processing service or queue broker.** Stronger isolation and scaling, but the pilot runs one process on one host (ADR-0021); child processes with timeouts and limits give isolation now, and a separate container is the deployment-level step in PJ-13.

title: Teluni Initial Release Requirements and Acceptance
heading: Scope and acceptance rules
text:
Scope and acceptance rules
**Decided:** complete the company-to-screen journey with tenant-safe remote management, images/videos, configurable data catalogs, freeform simultaneous content, regional schedules, offline Android TV playback and monitoring. The owner prioritizes intended product capability/quality over reducing scope solely to fit an MVP label. The historical `mvp.md` path remains the stable requirements entry point.
Every capability below is a requirement, not implemented functionality. The [plan](implementation-plan.md) owns delivery status; [release policies](release-policies.md) own business behavior and the questionnaire decision record; [acceptance targets](release-targets.md) own numeric limits and qualification goals. PH-09 policy/target selection is complete as of 2026-10-18. No hardware, pilot or performance qualification is inferred.
ID
Functional requirement
Required acceptance evidence before release
FR-01
Companies, branches, users, company settings, public company signup/automatic activation, authentication, scoped standard/custom profiles and temporary access
Two synthetic companies each have branches/users. Authorized members manage allowed resources; direct API attempts, lists/search, media/catalog access and identifier substitution cannot cross company/branch scope. Verify responsible-administrator approval, trusted account linking, strong/recent authentication, recovery, session bounds and 30-second revocation using [IA-01–IA-16](identity-and-access.md#required-verification-cases). Public activation must satisfy commercial/privacy/abuse gates; platform operation has no implicit customer-content access.
FR-02
Device identity, temporary-code pairing, company/branch assignment, name/configuration and safe unlink
An authorized user claims a displayed code once. Expired/replayed codes, concurrent claims, wrong-scope assignment and revoked identities fail safely. Reassignment requires verified cleanup/reset and cannot expose previous tenant data/credentials; unreachable erasure is shown as pending.
FR-03
Supported horizontal/vertical orientation
Qualified devices display supported orientations correctly; invalid geometry or unsupported profiles have explicit outcomes rather than silent support claims.
FR-04
Private image/video upload, validation, organization, metadata, reuse, conversion and reference-aware deletion
Approved profiles upload, validate/convert and play on tested hardware. Spoofed type, malformed/oversized content and unauthorized reads fail safely. Archive/deletion/retention preserve protected draft, active, staging and recovery references; assisted draft changes need confirmation.
FR-05
Playlists, ordered items, configurable image duration, full-video playback, looping, device/group assignment and qualified cuts/fades
Deterministic order and preview/player duration agreement. Devices have zero or one company-owned group, including cross-branch groups; explicit individual programming replaces the whole group source. Confirmed source changes use published content or an intentionally empty destination. Ordinary item completion and coordinated-page timing follow release policies.
FR-06
Dates, local hours, weekdays, overnight recurrence, regional schedules and deterministic conflict/no-match rules
Shared backend/player fixtures cover inclusive starts/exclusive ends, final-date clipping, all-day/equal-time validation, timezone/DST, overlapping same-output windows, regional exceptions and empty windows. Optional defaults otherwise give safe neutral output; expired commercial content is not an implicit fallback.
FR-07
Preview, publication, immutable consistent versions, desired/downloaded/active state and last-valid preservation
Ordinary drafts do not affect screens. Authorized price saves automatically publish affected published bindings through durable/retry-safe intent, excluding unrelated drafts. Concurrent/repeated operations and unknown outcomes are reconcilable. Complete supported versions activate only after validated staging; failures never replace valid state with mixed/corrupt resources.
FR-08
Android TV playback, bounded offline operation and controlled recovery/update
Qualified devices play local media/catalog snapshots without normal backend streaming, through the selected offline/clock/authorization envelope, reboot, power interruption and protocol/update cases in playback acceptance. Expired authorization or untrusted time has an explicit safe outcome.
FR-09
Scoped connection/last-contact/app/storage/sync/playback diagnostics
Show observed timestamps, stale/offline thresholds and actual version states. Distinguish failed sync, regional rendering failure and lost contact from stopped playback. Reconnection reconciles state without leaking data or claiming unseen erasure.
FR-10
Freeform simultaneous composition, independent areas with optional coordinated pages, per-area schedules, multiple videos and configurable mixed audio
Users position/resize areas and preview copy/import/export of versioned textual layouts. An active regional schedule survives a global page change; coordinated areas follow the selected page timeline. Isolated area failure/no-match preserves unaffected geometry/output. Qualified rendering/audio profiles and pagination remain readable and work offline.
FR-11
User-defined typed catalogs, fields and records with layout bindings, including products/prices and weekly agendas
Users configure a non-product catalog as well as a product configuration. Validate schema/version evolution, scoped record/media references, branch price overrides and import boundaries. Data-driven views paginate without silent name/price clipping. Price publication/expiry and unavailable-item defaults work from consistent offline snapshots; customization cannot execute arbitrary code or cross tenant boundaries.
FR-12
Bounded public trial, contracted screen licenses, qualified quota admission and manually administered commercial authorization
[CP-01–CP-12](commercial-policies.md#required-commercial-verification) cover verified trial boundaries, fixed licenses/replacement, reserved capacity, safe expiry/grace/cancellation/export and separately authorized payment reconciliation. No billing from heartbeat, partial download cutoff, unlimited defaults, surprise charge or security-suspension bypass. PH-18/PH-19 qualify the offer; no gateway or automatic invoicing is required.
Managed campaigns remain future scope; scheduled content and published price-validity rules provide the initial promotion behavior without approving a separate campaign engine.

title: Teluni Initial Release Requirements and Acceptance
heading: Release acceptance journey
text:
Release acceptance journey
Establish two synthetic companies through verified enrollment with responsible administrators, differently scoped branches/operators and qualified Android TV devices. Exercise IA-01–IA-16 login/linking/recovery/session/revocation/approval/support cases and API/media/catalog allow/deny boundaries; no implicit platform content privilege.
Pair devices, create a cross-branch group and an explicit individual exception. Upload media; configure a custom weekly-agenda catalog and product/price configuration. Compose independent and coordinated areas, regional schedules and an optional default; preview and publish A.
Verify local multi-video/audio/catalog rendering under the qualified profile. Edit drafts without changing A. Save a price and verify automatic consistent publication from published dependencies without leaking unrelated drafts; test concurrent edits, duplicate delivery and failed/unknown outcomes.
Publish B while playback continues. Cut network/power at download/staging/activation boundaries and verify complete valid A or B. Isolate a runtime regional fault without confusing it with incomplete-generation activation. Check protected references and insufficient disk outcomes.
Exercise schedule/date/DST/promotion/no-match/pagination and regional-page timing offline. Test the trusted-clock and authorization deadlines, restart/recovery and the expected safe neutral states.
Reconnect and reconcile observed state. Unlink/revoke while offline, then verify cleanup before cross-company pairing. Exercise historical recovery without expired offers or resurrected credentials and validate controlled protocol/app updates.
Exercise CP-01–CP-12 commercial trial/license/quota, reconciled-payment and grace/cancellation cases, preserving independent identity permission and valid offline deadlines. Rehearse database-plus-media restore and endpoint migration in isolation. Record target-linked load/usability/hardware evidence, customer acceptance, real costs/support coverage and residual risk before real-customer acceptance; billing readiness remains PH-19.
Evidence includes automated contract/security/integration/browser tests, representative hardware/power/network tests, restore results and user observation. Delivery can be incremental; an operational release requires the complete applicable acceptance set. Passing foundation validation only checks currently implemented foundation/docs.

Explicitly outside the MVP
The historical heading remains a stable route; initial scope now includes freeform composition, configurable catalogs and their approved commercial defaults. Further unreviewed widgets, managed campaigns, external ERP/POS/partner integration APIs/webhooks/imports, automated billing/payment-gateway subscriptions, white-label, AI, playback analytics, general remote-control tools, impersonation, synchronization across separate screens and alternative players remain future unless independently approved. PH-11 separately selects scoped consent-based human support, custom access profiles and optional independent publication approvals for the initial release; custom profiles exist for the current organization capabilities, and the other policies remain unimplemented. Generic fields do not approve arbitrary executable plugins, unrestricted data collection or all roadmap capabilities.

text:
Constraints and current state
**Decided constraint:** no present cloud-service budget. The owner intends to use a personal residential server for development, tests and potentially initial customers, moving to a VPS/cloud when revenue or operational need justifies it. **Accepted initial architecture under ADR-0021:** Debian Linux, Docker Compose, a reverse proxy with HTTPS, local persistent media, automated backups and suitable monitoring. Real-customer use remains subject to PH-10 readiness gates. None is a deployed Teluni environment or executable procedure in this repository.
Follow inherited [production access](../security/production-access.md), [secrets management](../security/secrets-management.md), [retention](../security/data-retention.md), [observability](../reliability/observability.md), [alerting](../reliability/alerting.md), and [runbook authoring](../runbooks/authoring.md). This plan does not grant production authority. Write tested deployment/recovery runbooks when the environment exists, rather than speculative commands now.
